Extract the residuals of a fitted model

Source: R/model-classes.R, R/model-rf.R
spatial_fit-residuals.Rd

residuals() on a random forest, a GWR or a Bayesian GP fit returns the observed response minus fitted(), one value per training row:

  • for a random forest these are out-of-bag residuals, since its fitted values are out-of-bag predictions. Out-of-bag is a random hold-out: use cv_rf() on folds at the distances the map will be used at for the forest's accuracy;

  • for a GWR they are in-sample. Where fit_gwr_model() took the response about its centre (a response at a large offset), the response and the fitted values are both taken about that centre, so the residuals keep digits that rounding at the response's size would lose (see "The local solve" in ?fit_gwr_model);

  • for a Bayesian GP they are in-sample, from the cached posterior expectation (spatial_fit-fitted).

residual_morans_i() tests them for spatial structure the model did not capture.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'gwr_fit'
residuals(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bayesian_fit'
residuals(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rf_fit'
residuals(object, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted rf_fit, gwr_fit or bayesian_fit.

...

Not used.

Value

A numeric vector of length object$n.

See also

residual_morans_i().

Other fit methods: plot.spatial_fit(), print.spatial_fit(), spatial_fit-coef, spatial_fit-fitted, spatial_fit-predict, summary.spatial_fit()

Examples

library(sf)
set.seed(1)
pts <- st_as_sf(
  data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(60, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(60, 0, 1000),
             a = rnorm(60)),
  coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632
)
pts$z <- 10 + 2 * pts$a + rnorm(60, 0, 0.3)
rf <- fit_rf_model(pts, "z", "a", num_trees = 50, seed = 1)
summary(residuals(rf))   # out-of-bag residuals
#>       Min.    1st Qu.     Median       Mean    3rd Qu.       Max. 
#> -0.9261726 -0.2510723  0.0065013  0.0008667  0.3091709  0.9810524
